root_cause: Independent Opus High report 14 (97a41235) rejected the r7 sentence-per-cue script proposal for six blockers: R7-1 sentence 16 asserts that no field result exists where the source says only that the article reports none, R7-2 the 98.82 percent validation figure sits beside the hub model and reads as the hub model result when the source ties it to the on-device TinyML AI, R7-3 the script grows to 163 words and 18 sentences while both boards keep a 58.7 s runtime and contiguous clause windows so the measured read overruns the scenes, R7-4 events at width 0.32 on n1b, n3b and n5c project past the 1.2 s limit, R7-5 (artistic, blocking) the per-sentence shot split produced same-view cuts in A s5 and B s6 and s7, R7-6 the close direction points at line 8 which is now a different read and verification metadata describes the old script. D1 (take 6 misread), D2 (caption fit unmeasured) and D3 (event timing) remain open from report 13, D4 is resolved by the proposal and D5 stays a process observation.
repair: Replace the rejected r7 bytes with immutable R8 proposals: attribute the figure to the on-device TinyML AI and the university in the sentence itself, replace the absolute no-field-result sentence with a reports-none statement tied to the university, compute a measured-rate runtime projection and trim or retime so clause windows hold the read, size every event width to at most 1.2 s over the projected clause length, give each same-view pair a different useful framing with a continuous transition or merge it, and refresh direction and verification metadata. Both treatments are renewed through the same two authored asset groups.
mechanism_change: The caption lever moves from in-sentence silent beats to one complete sentence per cue split at full-stop gaps, with projected clause windows, event widths sized from measured read rates and varied framing.
expected_visible_result: One continuous take whose sentences each fit one two-line caption cue at 40 px or more, every event between 0.2 s and 1.2 s inside its spoken clause, no figure attached to the wrong model, no same-view cuts, and both treatments presented as a fresh silent comparison.
